dailyFacts.title: Axolotl Complete Organ Regeneration
dailyFacts.fact: The axolotl salamander can regrow lost limbs, crushed spines, and parts of its heart, retina, and brain without scar tissue. Transplanted organs from other axolotls are accepted without any immune rejection.
dailyFacts.source: Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics

dailyFacts.title: Alaskan Wood Frog Frozen Hibernation
dailyFacts.fact: The Alaskan wood frog survives sub-zero winters by freezing 70% of its body water solid. Its heart completely stops beating and brain activity ceases for months, thawed unharmed when spring arrives via high-concentration glucose antifreeze.

dailyFacts.title: Bumblebee Electrostatic Foraging
dailyFacts.fact: Bumblebees build up positive electric charges as they fly. Because flowers possess a slight negative charge, pollen grains literally jump through the air onto the bee’s body, and the altered electric field signals to arriving bees that the flower was recently visited.

dailyFacts.title: Blue Whale Vascular Dimensions
dailyFacts.fact: A blue whale’s main aorta is over 9 inches in diameter—large enough for a toddler to crawl through. Its heart weighs approximately 400 pounds (the size of a small golf cart), and its heartbeat can be detected by acoustic sensors over two miles away underwater.

dailyFacts.title: Crow Facial Recognition & Grudges
dailyFacts.fact: Corvids (crows and ravens) remember individual human faces for decades. When a human treats a crow aggressively, the crow transmits that person’s description to the entire flock and teaches subsequent generations to identify and mob that specific human.

thoughtOfTheDay.title: Tat Tvam Asi (Recognizing the Infinite Within)
thoughtOfTheDay.quote: तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो — You are That, O Shvetaketu.
thoughtOfTheDay.reflection: When external social comparison tries to measure your worth by follower counts or peer achievements, step back. Your fundamental consciousness is unborn, complete, and boundless. Work with joy from fullness, not from a sense of lack.
